source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten structured references: the Cahill SSI paper, Ports/Grittner PostgreSQL implementation paper, Fekete SI theory, Adya dependency theory, current PostgreSQL 18 isolation, predicate-lock configuration, pg_locks, system-information documentation, the PostgreSQL SSI project wiki, and the SSN primary paper. Every final destination was retrieved and retained; current claims are scoped to PostgreSQL 18 and distinguished from the general SSI theorem.

evidence: Checked Ti, wr, ww, rw antidependency, serialization graph, dangerous structure, false positive/negative, predicate marker, promotion, safe snapshot, and safe retry definitions.
Checked every rw edge uses reader-to-later-writer direction and the theorem consistently permits T1=T3 for a two-transaction cycle.
Checked commit rank uses smaller rank as earlier and equality only for the T1=T3 identity case.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Dependency and commit-order notation is consistent across prose, executable evidence, examples, exercises, and answers.

evidence: Recomputed the two-vertex write-skew graph: edges T1->T2 and T2->T1 are cyclic and yield witness (T1,T2,T1) when T1 commits first.
Recomputed the three-vertex chain A->B->C with C first: it has witness (A,B,C) and remains acyclic.
Independently enumerated 64 directed three-vertex graphs across six commit orders: all 234 cyclic cases had a local witness, while 24 of 150 acyclic cases also had one.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The enumeration verifies the finite graph/witness implementation and necessity-versus-sufficiency distinction; it does not encode all SI history constraints.

evidence: Reviewed the contradiction proof: nonserializable SI implies a cycle, every such cycle has a qualified dangerous structure, and sound prevention of all such structures therefore excludes every cycle.
Verified the converse is not asserted: adjacent rw edges need not have a closing T3-to-T1 path.
Derived the read-only ordering rule: the incoming edge to read-only T1 must be wr, placing its writer before T1's snapshot, and earliest-committer T3 therefore precedes that snapshot.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The full SI theorem is attributed to primary research; the chapter supplies a scoped proof structure and the complete read-only derivation, not an independent reproof of every multiversion lemma.

evidence: Reviewed two versus three transactions, T1=T3, same/disjoint writes, tuple versus empty predicate, exact versus coarse access, cyclic versus acyclic dangerous structures, and simultaneous commit boundaries.
Reviewed read/write versus read-only, ordinary versus safe versus deferrable snapshots, prompt start versus startup wait, and safe retry versus guaranteed eventual success.

Reviewed subtransaction abort, prepared/in-doubt state, crash/recovery, metadata after commit, promotion/summarization, new access methods, replicas/caches, external side effects, cancellation, and ambiguous commit.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Unsupported implementation details remain explicit proof obligations rather than assumed PostgreSQL behavior.

evidence: Checked edge completeness covers values and absences, edge direction follows visibility, commit checks precede irrevocability, and no committed victim is selected.
Checked retained/summarized state remains until no overlapping transaction can need it and every promotion is a coverage superset.

Checked application invariants require complete serializable participation, discarded aborted results, whole-transaction retry, stable operation identity, and transactional external-effect integration.
invariant_checking.notes: False positives affect precision/liveness; false negatives violate the serializability safety claim.

evidence: Reviewed serialization-graph acyclicity, SI visibility/version constraints, adjacent-rw theorem statement, overlap corollary, earliest-committer qualification, and conservative prevention argument.
Reviewed predicate coverage, atomic commit resolution, victim removal, safe-retry rationale, retention, and recovery as implementation premises.
Reviewed safe-snapshot construction and why read-only status alone does not exclude anomaly participation.
proof_review.notes: Exact PostgreSQL conflict-state structures, atomics, WAL records, and recovery code are outside the chapter and are not claimed verified.

evidence: The dangerous-structure theorem is attributed and separated from the finite graph checker.
The executable explicitly disclaims snapshot/version/predicate and production scheduler coverage.
PostgreSQL 18 observations, general SSI properties, conservative implementation choices, operational recommendations, and historical benchmark claims are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter neither labels every MVCC serializable implementation SSI nor treats every serialization failure as proof of an actual application anomaly.

evidence: The repository verifier passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact eight-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and recorded Python toolchain evidence.
Independent enumeration checked 384 graph/commit-order cases and recorded counts plus chain/cycle boundary results in artifacts/reviews/DBE-049/independent-recomputation.txt.
All ten final reference destinations and every repository-local link were retrieved or resolved.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live PostgreSQL SSI schedule, alternative engine, access-plan change, memory promotion, prepared transaction, crash recovery, replica, driver/pool, benchmark, or production workload was empirically tested.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the progression from multiversion edges through the dangerous-structure theorem, conservative detection, predicates, bounded memory, post-commit state, victim choice, safe snapshots, false positives, application retry, and verification. Model, theorem, implementation, configuration, and policy remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed SIREAD nonblocking semantics, index/scan precision, predicate settings, tracking retention, prepared/subtransaction/recovery concerns, safe-retry limitations, deferrable reports, SQLSTATE 40001 handling, idempotency/outbox, privacy-safe metrics, capacity controls, and rollout schedules.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter retrieves DBE-048's anomaly, derives why SSI works, contrasts one cyclic and one acyclic witness, teaches necessary-not-sufficient reasoning, includes twelve misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete corrective answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, PostgreSQL/SSI/SSN maintainer, database-vendor, standards, security, performance, reliability, operations, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite graph enumeration prove neither the full SI dangerous-structure theorem independently, complete predicate/version-history inference, correctness of PostgreSQL internals or configuration, absence of false negatives in a production engine, prepared/recovery/replica correctness, application transaction completeness, strict serializability, external-system atomicity, universal retry progress, workload-independent performance, certification, nor deployment fitness.
